title: Grateful Dead Live at Golden Hall Community Concourse on 1970-08-05
lineage: SBD > MR > Reel > PCM > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: A rare acoustic August‑5‑1970 show shines with stellar renditions (El Paso, Ballad of Casey Jones, Cocaine Blues) despite a hissy, muddy soundboard tape.
ai_review.review: This recording captures one of the most treasured all‑acoustic Dead performances from summer ’70, featuring standout numbers like El Paso, Rosalie McFall, Cocaine Blues and a haunting Ballad of Casey Jones. Reviewers rave about the relaxed, almost church‑like vibe and the rare mandolin work (David Nelson or possibly Jerry). The soundboard source is plagued by hiss, a muddy mix and low vocals, but the musical magic more than compensates for the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews praise the performance and rare song selections (70% weight), while noting consistent recording issues such as hiss and a muddy mix (30% weight). The balance yields an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hissy tape, muddy mid‑range, mandolin mixed too high, vocals often buried, occasional drop‑outs; nevertheless the source captures the acoustic ambience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A laid‑back, almost worship‑like acoustic set that flows through folk, gospel and early‑70 country‑rock material; rare tunes are woven in seamlessly.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar work is praised throughout; a mandolin presence (either Jerry or guest David Nelson) is highlighted as a beautiful bonus.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as restrained and supportive, giving the acoustic set just enough weight.
band_member_comments.Drums: Debate over whether Mickey or Kreutzmann is on drums; some feel the drum mix is too forward or out of balance.
